text: Git branching is a key part of modern version control. When you work on a project, you often need to add new features without breaking the main code. That is why developers create feature branches. A feature branch is a separate copy of the project where you can make changes safely. Once your work is ready, you can merge it back into the main branch. Before merging, many teams use pull requests. A pull request lets other people review your code and discuss it before it becomes part of the project. This workflow keeps the main branch clean and helps teams work together without conflicts.
